title: The Geometry of LLM-as-Judge: Why Inter-LLM Consensus Is Not Human Alignment
zh_title: 以大模型为裁判的几何学：为何裁判间共识并不等于与人类对齐
authors: Sourabrata Mukherjee, Hamna Hamna, Kalika Bali, Sunayana Sitaram
abstract: LLM judges now score most open-ended NLP output, and their mutual agreement is routinely read as evidence that the scores can be trusted. That reading is unsafe: judges may agree because they capture quality, or because they share the same blind spots, and agreement statistics alone cannot tell these apart. We develop a geometric test that can. Treating each judge's scores as a vector, we measure spread, effective rank, the angle to human scores, and the judge-judge, judge-human, and human-human agreement triple for 42 judges on two community-built Indic benchmarks covering four domains and eight languages. Every comparison is reference-matched: a judge and a held-out rater are scored against the same two-rater mean, since an averaged reference otherwise flatters judges by several degrees. On subjective rubrics, judges agree with one another as much as humans do yet reach only 58-66% of human agreement and often concentrate on an axis humans do not weight. On the one rubric with a verifiable answer, most of that gap closes. Ensembles converge on the judges' shared axis rather than the human one, and training widens scores without rotating them. Inter-judge agreement is evidence of human alignment only after this check passes.
zh_abstract: 如今，开放式 NLP 输出的打分大多由大模型裁判完成，裁判之间的相互一致常被当作分数可信的证据。本文指出这种读法并不安全：裁判达成一致，既可能因为捕捉到了质量，也可能因为共享同一片盲区，而一致性统计量无法区分二者。为此我们提出一种几何检验：把每个裁判的分数视为向量，测量其展布、有效秩、与人类分数的夹角，以及裁判—裁判、裁判—人类、人类—人类的一致性三元组，对象为 42 个裁判、两个社区构建的印度语系基准，覆盖 4 个领域、8 种语言。所有比较都做参考匹配——裁判与留出的人类评分者对着相同的两位评分者均值计分——因为改用平均参考会把裁判抬高好几个角度。结果显示：在主观评分维度上，裁判彼此的一致程度与人类相当，却只达到人类一致性的 58%–66%，且集中在一条人类并不加权的共享轴上；在唯一可核验的维度上，这一差距大部分闭合。集成收敛到裁判共享的轴，训练只拉宽分数而不转动方向。结论是，裁判间一致性只有在几何检验通过之后，才算得上是与人类对齐的证据。
citation: [117] Mukherjee S, Hamna, Bali K, Sitaram S. The geometry of LLM-as-judge: Why inter-LLM consensus is not human alignment[J]. arXiv preprint arXiv:2606.03043, 2026. [arXiv]
